title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence Into The Skill Development Ecosystem
body_text:
The Government has systematically integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the national skilling ecosystem through the following measures:
Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH)
Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) has been launched as a unified Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and serves as the core platform for technology-driven skilling. Under SIDH, the Ministry launched the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) programme on 22.07.2025 to promote AI literacy and prepare learners for an AI-enabled future. The programme initially comprised four fully online, self-paced, NSQF-aligned and credit-linked foundational learner courses – AI to be Aware, AI to Acquire, AI to Aspire, and AI for Educators. The programme was subsequently expanded to include 50 AI and AI application-oriented qualifications covering AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualised AI applications for the unorganised sector. As on 06.08.2026, a total of 5,17,477 learners have enrolled and 1,00,664 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on SIDH.
Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, emphasis has been placed on industry-aligned and future-ready skills, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Data Science, Internet of Things (IoT), Cyber Security, Cloud Computing, Semiconductors, Drones, Electric Vehicles (EVs), Green Hydrogen, Robotics, AR/VR and 5G Technologies. The scheme framework incorporates demand-driven skilling, enhanced industry participation, mandatory On-the-Job Training (OJT) in applicable job roles, promotion of apprenticeship opportunities, and strengthened digital monitoring mechanisms through the Skill India ecosystem. As per SIDH reports up to 30.06.2026, under PMKVY 4.0, 5,44,383 candidates have been trained/oriented and 3,73,766 candidates certified in future-skills job roles.
The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) promotes apprenticeship training through industry-led, on-the-job learning, including in emerging and future-ready sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Robotics, Cyber Security, Data Analytics and Green Jobs. Apprenticeship opportunities are also available in AI, Machine Learning, Semiconductors, Electric Vehicles, Drones, Renewable Energy and other technology-driven areas through participation of industry and Sector Skill Councils. Under NAPS, 3,175 apprentices have been engaged and 855 apprentices certified in AI and Machine Learning-related job roles during the last three years.
ITI Upgradation Scheme
Directorate General of Training (DGT) implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), under which craftsmen training is provided in 170 NSQF-aligned trades. At present, there are 13,856 ITIs in the country, comprising 3,328 Government ITIs and 10,528 Private ITIs.
DGT has introduced Artificial Intelligence (AI) into vocational training by developing the Artificial Intelligence Programming Assistant (AIPA) course of one-year duration, a 240-hour Generative AI course, and a 7.5-hour AI micro-credential for trainees in ITIs. The compulsory Employability Skills curriculum has also been revised to include modules on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Green Skills. The AIPA course under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) is being conducted at 23 National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) across the country.
The Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme at an estimated cost of ₹60,000 crore (Central Share: ₹30,000 crore, State Share: ₹20,000 crore and Industry Share: ₹10,000 crore) for upgradation of 1,000 ITIs through hub-and-spoke arrangements in collaboration with State Governments and industry. Under this scheme, an industry-led Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is provided the necessary autonomy to propose modifications in the curriculum by introducing new courses and upgrading existing courses as per industry requirements, including in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, cloud computing, data analytics, robotics, the Internet of Things (IoT), and other Industry 4.0 technologies.
Further, the Ministry has issued 'Guidelines for Empanelment of Centre of Excellence – Skills (CoE-Skills) and Vocational Training Centres (VTC)', which provide for advanced, technology-enabled training delivery — including Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled infrastructure, digital learning tools and emerging technology labs across identified sectors — to support future-ready and industry-aligned skill training.
The National Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NPAI) Skilling Framework, notified by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) on 25.09.2023, provides a national framework for AI skilling through a three-tiered approach comprising AI for All, AI for Many and AI for the Few. The framework envisages structured AI learning pathways, aligned with industry requirements, to support AI-enabled skilling, workforce development and lifelong learning, including for diverse learner groups and sectors of the economy.
At present, there are 119 NSQF-aligned and NSQC-approved qualifications related to Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML) and Data Science. These include the four foundational AI learning courses and 50 AI and AI application-oriented NSQF-aligned courses launched under the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) programme. The courses are delivered through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) by NCVET-recognised Awarding Bodies. As per the SOAR Dashboard on SIDH, as on 06.08.2026, 5,17,477 learners have enrolled and 1,00,664 learners have successfully completed and been certified under the SOAR programme.
From Data available on Skill India Digital Hub, the State-wise/UT-wise details of candidates trained/oriented and certified in AI, Machine Learning and Data Science-related job roles under PMKVY 4.0, enrolment in New Age Courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) during the last three years, and apprentices engaged and certified in AI and Machine Learning-related job roles under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), including Odisha, are at Annexure-I .
The Government has undertaken several measures to ensure effective access to digital skilling platforms, including the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), for citizens across rural, remote and aspirational districts. SIDH serves as a one-stop digital platform for accessing skilling, certification, apprenticeship and employment-related opportunities through a single interface.
As per Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) reports up to 30.06.2026, under PMKVY 4.0, 3,730 candidates have been trained/oriented and 2,651 candidates certified in AI-related job roles in Aspirational Districts, and 3,435 candidates have been trained/oriented and 2,331 candidates certified in AI-related job roles in Tribal Districts.

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship informed the Rajya Sabha about steps to integrate Artificial Intelligence into India's skilling ecosystem, including the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), the SOAR programme, PMKVY 4.0, NAPS, ITI upgradation via AI courses, and the PM-SETU scheme. As of August 2026, over 5.17 lakh learners enrolled and 1.006 lakh certified under SOAR, while PMKVY 4.0 has trained 5.44 lakh and certified 3.73 lakh candidates in future-skills roles. State-wise data show Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh leading in AI-related training and certification.
enrichment.context:
India's skilling architecture has been evolving to address disruption from automation and AI by embedding future-ready skills into flagship schemes like PMKVY, NAPS, and the Craftsmen Training Scheme run through ITIs. The Skill India Digital Hub, launched as a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), exemplifies India's broader DPI strategy (similar to Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker) of creating unified digital platforms for public service delivery, in this case linking skilling, certification, apprenticeship and employment. The National Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NPAI) Skilling Framework and its three-tiered approach (AI for All, AI for Many, AI for the Few) mirrors global efforts to build layered AI literacy—from basic awareness to specialized talent—necessary for economic competitiveness.

The recently approved PM-SETU scheme (₹60,000 crore) reflects a shift toward industry co-financed and industry-governed vocational training via Special Purpose Vehicles, aiming to make India's 13,856 ITIs more responsive to Industry 4.0 needs such as AI, robotics, IoT and cybersecurity. This has implications for the demographic dividend debate: India's youthful workforce needs continuous upskilling to remain employable as AI transforms job markets, and government interventions in Aspirational and Tribal Districts aim to ensure such transformation is inclusive rather than exacerbating regional and social disparities.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR)' programme is delivered through which of the following platforms?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that SOAR is a programme launched under the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), which serves as the core Digital Public Infrastructure for technology-driven skilling.

prelims_questions.question: The PM-SETU scheme, aimed at upgrading 1,000 ITIs, involves financial contributions from which of the following?
options: Central Government and State Governments only
Central Government, State Governments, and Industry
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PM-SETU has an estimated cost of ₹60,000 crore shared as Central Share ₹30,000 crore, State Share ₹20,000 crore, and Industry Share ₹10,000 crore.
